subject: Staged receivables ladder, credit cap, and VAT pass-through - Stellargo
messages:
From: Marcus Dunn <marcus.dunn@stellargo.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellargo.com>, Stellargo Finance <finance@stellargo.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Flex on terms / request for proposal

Alex —

Following our call this morning, we need a written proposal that lets us pilot at scale while mitigating our cashflow hiccups. High level asks from our side: a staged payment ladder (so we can sync payments to customer billing), some temporary credit (to cover month 1–2 burst usage), and clarity on VAT handling since we operate across multiple EU jurisdictions.

Can you outline what Redwood can offer for a 6‑month pilot with expected spend ~€180k/month and a possible ramp to €350k/month? We need a short doc and an invoice cadence we can show procurement.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Dunn
Head of Platform Ops, Stellargo
marcus.dunn@stellargo.com

[Attachment: none]
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Dunn <marcus.dunn@stellargo.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellargo.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:40:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Flex on terms / request for proposal

Marcus — thanks for the call. Draft proposal attached; summary below and I included an example invoice cadence + sample invoice.

Summary (proposal):
- Pilot length: 6 months
- Billing cadence: monthly invoices, Net45 standard for pilot, with staged receivables ladder to smooth large month‑over‑month changes
- Upfront: 25% initial deposit invoice (covers onboarding + first 2 weeks of usage)
- Ladder: remaining 75% billed monthly but split into two tranches per month: 60% due Net45, 40% deferred to Net75 and collected as usage stabilizes (deferred tranche applies only for the first 3 months)
- Credit cap: temporary unsecured credit line of €250,000 for the pilot period (review at month 3)
- VAT/tax: Redwood will invoice gross with VAT where applicable; we propose pass‑through treatment with Stellargo required to provide local VAT registration or tax certificate for reverse‑charge where appropriate. If withholding is required by local law, we ask for documentation and gross‑up language so Redwood receives full contracted USD/EUR.
- Early‑pay incentive: 1.0% discount on invoice if paid within Net15.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposal_StagedReceivables_20261117.pdf, Redwood_Invoice_20261101.pdf (sample).

Next steps: if that structure looks close, we can prepare a PO‑friendly one‑page SOW and a DocuSign amendment to the Master Services Agreement. I can also loop finance for the credit approval.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

[Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_StagedReceivables_20261117.pdf (proposal, 48KB); Redwood_Invoice_20261101.pdf (sample invoice, 35KB)]
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellargo.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Dunn <marcus.dunn@stellargo.com>, Stellargo Finance <finance@stellargo.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T07:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Flex on terms / request for proposal

Alex —

Thanks for the quick turn. A couple of clarifying items from procurement/tax:

1) Net terms: Procurement prefers Net30 for operational suppliers during pilots to align cashflow. Could Redwood do Net30 on the non‑deferred tranche and Net60 for the deferred tranche? That reduces our credit ask and helps our AP team.

2) Credit cap: €250k is a good start but if we ramp to €350k/month we will need the cushion to scale. Could we structure a review at 30 days with an automatic increase to €400k if usage triggers are met (e.g., sustained 30% MoM increase)?

3) VAT: We can provide the EU VAT registration & tax certificate (attached). However, for a few countries we operate through local resellers, and withholding can apply. Would Redwood accept a gross‑up clause if we can provide legal guidance that withholding applies? We need a straightforward clause in the amendment that allows for local withholding without reducing Redwood’s contracted receipts.

I attached our tax cert for your review.

Elena Torres
Director, Procurement — Stellargo
elena.torres@stellargo.com

[Attachment: Stellargo_Tax_Cert_2026.pdf (tax certificate, 12KB)]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellargo.com>, Marcus Dunn <marcus.dunn@stellargo.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Flex on terms / request for proposal

Hi Elena / Marcus — looping in finance and legal from Redwood to lock this down. A few operational clarifications and a suggested final structure: 

- Terms: we can accept Net30 on the primary (60%) tranche and Net60 on the deferred (40%) tranche for the first 3 months. After month 3 we transition to a single Net45 on full monthly invoices unless both parties agree otherwise.
- Credit cap and scale: we will provision an initial credit cap of €300,000 (up from Alex's €250k) with an automatic review and prescribed increase to €450,000 on meeting both a usage trigger (sustained 25% MoM growth over 2 consecutive months) and a credit review (basic financial questionnaire + recent AR aging). The cap increase will be effective 7 business days after confirmation.
- VAT/withholding: Redwood will invoice gross. If local law requires withholding, Redwood requests either (a) a gross‑up clause so Redwood receives the contracted amount net of withholding, or (b) Stellargo to provide tax receipts/evidence within 30 days so Redwood can claim treaty relief/credits. We accept the Stellargo tax cert as valid for reverse charge in jurisdictions where that applies — Redwood will adjust invoices accordingly where reverse‑charge is supported by local law and documentation is provided prior to the invoice date.
- Operational asks: please have finance confirm the billing contact, PO number cadence, and whether payments will be made centralized from your EU treasury or by local entities (affects VAT).

I attached a short amendment template (embedded in the proposal Alex shared) that reflects these points; we can fast‑track a DocuSign if you confirm the credit cap and Net terms.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

[Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_StagedReceivables_20261117.pdf (amendment excerpt, 6KB)]
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@stellargo.com>, Marcus Dunn <marcus.dunn@stellargo.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Stellargo Finance <finance@stellargo.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Flex on terms / request for proposal

Elena / Marcus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Confirming agreed pilot billing mechanics below so we can send the DocuSign: 

1) Billing cadence: monthly invoices during pilot (invoice date = 1st of each month)
2) Payment terms: Primary tranche (60%) Net30; Deferred tranche (40%) Net60 for months 1–3. From month 4 onward, single monthly invoice Net45 unless amended in writing.
3) Upfront: 25% deposit invoice due Net15 (covers onboarding).
4) Credit cap: initial €300,000; automatic increase to €450,000 upon meeting usage trigger + credit review as described by Rishi.
4) VAT/Withholding: Redwood invoices gross. Stellargo to provide VAT registration/tax certificate for reverse‑charge where applicable (we received Stellargo_Tax_Cert_2026.pdf). If local withholding applies, we will include a gross‑up clause in the amendment to preserve Redwood’s contracted receipts; alternatively, Stellargo may provide withholding receipts within 30 days for Redwood to claim relief.
5) Early pay: 1.0% discount for payments settled within Net15.

Please confirm and reply with the correct PO name/number and the AP contact. Once confirmed I will route the DocuSign and loop in our provisioning team to standby for capacity.

Thanks — look forward to getting this live.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
